info.name: TCOS Finance Tracking — Auth (chompoo)
info.description:
For a single unattended Collection Runner pass across ALL domains, use `TCOS-Full-Suite.postman_collection.json` instead — it merges this collection (minus the Supabase-dependent requests) with the other 3.

The 9 auth endpoints owned by chompoo — POST /auth/login, /logout, /refresh, GET /auth/me, POST /auth/password/forgot, /password/reset, /claim, /login/supabase, /verify-password.

All real (non-mock) as of this collection — every request here hits the actual `staff` table via Postgres, regardless of MOCK_MODE (which only still applies to the other 6 domains). See api/README.md and docs/backend/03-api-spec.md §4.

**Before this can succeed against a live server** you need a reachable Postgres with the `staff` table (local `supabase start`, or the hosted project once its schema is pushed) AND at least one seeded `staff` row. See the collection-level `Setup notes` request for the full checklist.

Run order for the happy path: Login → Get Me → Verify Password (step-up) → Refresh → Logout. Claim / Login via Supabase / Forgot / Reset are separate flows, run independently.

request.description:
Not an auth endpoint — just a harmless request to hang these notes on.

To run this collection for real you need, in order:

1. A reachable Postgres with the shipped schema applied — either `npm run supabase:start` (local Docker) from the repo root, or the hosted project (already live as of this collection). Point `api/.env`'s DB_HOST/DB_PORT at whichever one you're using.
2. At least one row in `staff` with a real email — added by an admin (there's no self-signup endpoint by design). The seed data has 6 (4 already claimed, 2 not).
3. For Claim / Login via Supabase specifically: a matching Supabase Auth user (`auth.users`, same email) — separate system from our own `staff` table. Run "7b. Get Supabase session (dev helper)" to mint a real token directly in Postman (no manual token-copying needed); see that request's description for how to create the Supabase Auth user itself if it doesn't exist yet.
4. Plain email+password Login only needs step 1 + 2, plus running Claim once (or inserting a bcrypt hash directly) to give that staff row a password_hash.

request.description: #4 — real Staff row by the token's sub. `scope` (department memberships) still comes from the mock-mode permissive scope — that's shared authorization infra outside these 9 endpoints, see docs/backend/04-authorization.md §2.

#59 — step-up re-auth (doc 04 §9). Real bcrypt.compare against the current staff row. Returns a 5-min `reauth_token` for X-Reauth-Token on sensitive actions (payment approve, reimbursement status change, signature upload).

#3 — no body, no Authorization header: relies entirely on the refresh_token cookie Postman captured from Login (its cookie jar replays it automatically for the same host even though it's HttpOnly). Verifies the cookie is really typ:"refresh" and reloads the live staff row before reissuing a session.
#2 — clears the refresh_token cookie. Requires a currently-valid access token; doesn't touch the DB.

#5 — always returns the same generic message regardless of whether the email exists (doc 03 §4). No email provider is wired up yet, so on a real match the server LOGS the reset link instead of sending it — copy the `reset_token` out of the API server's console output and paste it into the next request's `reset_token` variable.

#6 — set the `reset_token` collection variable from the server log first (see request 6). Existing access/refresh tokens for that staff member are NOT invalidated by this — there's no session store yet (doc 02 §6), a known real gap.

request.description:
NOT one of the 9 auth endpoints — hits Supabase's own Auth API directly (GoTrue password grant), not our backend, to mint a real Supabase session for the next two requests. Sets `supabase_access_token` automatically.

Requires a real Supabase Auth user (`auth.users`) for `supabase_email` — separate from our own `staff` table. Create one with SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY:
```
POST {{supabase_url}}/auth/v1/admin/users
Authorization: Bearer <SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY>
apikey: <SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY>
{ "email": "...", "password": "...", "email_confirm": true }
```
Supabase Auth's password here is independent of our own `staff.password_hash` — they don't need to match. Session tokens expire in ~1hr (project's jwt_expiry), so re-run this whenever Claim/Login via Supabase start 401ing with an expired token.

#57 — the Authorization header here is a SUPABASE session access_token, not one of ours (this route deliberately doesn't accept our Bearer tokens). Run "7b. Get Supabase session" first to populate `supabase_access_token` — point `supabase_email` at a staff row that's NOT claimed yet (password_hash NULL — e.g. fah@tcos.app or ploy@tcos.app in the seed data) or this 409s ALREADY_CLAIMED. Fails NOT_PROVISIONED if no `staff` row matches that email at all.

#58 — alternate login for an already-claimed account via a Supabase session token (same `supabase_access_token` variable as Claim, from "7b. Get Supabase session"). Point `supabase_email` at a staff row that already HAS a password_hash (e.g. titiporn02468@gmail.com / golf@tcos.app) or this 404s ACCOUNT_NOT_CLAIMED.
